page: Microsoft Azure FX48mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine engineered for demanding computational tasks that require massive memory footprints. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The allocation provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix capabilities including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 instruction sets.

The system is provisioned with 1008.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is addressed through an onboard 2832 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency local scratch and caching capacity. There are no discrete hardware GPUs attached to this instance, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark outcomes show high computational throughput across multiple domains. Single-core performance achieved a Geekbench score of 2338.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, while the multi-core score reached 20347.0. The PassMark CPU test recorded 70724.12 points, alongside extended instruction testing at 75791.68 points. Memory bandwidth is prominent, registering 330.82 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 158.98 GB/sec for large write blocks. Data manipulation tests show 74.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 77.33 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

While general stress-ng benchmarks position both single-core (2168.28) and multi-core (53295.74) compute in the middle 50 percent, the instance demonstrates high performance in specialized execution paths. Without dedicated accelerators, large LLM text generation slows to 3.45 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model, reflecting the expected limitations of pure CPU inference. However, prompt processing remains competitive via AMX acceleration. The high proportion of memory to compute makes the instance efficient for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and data analytics pipelines.

Accompanied by a substantial 1008.0 GB RAM allocation (21.0 GB per vCPU) and a 2832 GB local NVMe SSD, it provides high-throughput memory execution with 330.82 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Hardware features include AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. In benchmarks, the server ranks within the top percentiles for single-core Geekbench performance (2338.0), Redis SET processing (74.99 million ops/sec), and text processing. Without dedicated GPUs, heavy model generation is constrained, but prompt processing and database operations remain fast. The configuration serves in-memory databases, electronic design automation, batch financial analysis, and large-scale compilation workloads.
